info.title: rial API
info.description: Prove a photo is real. Base URL: https://api.rial.io

tags.name: Verifications
tags.description: Create, fetch, list, and finalize verifications. The core of the API — every tenant integration starts here.

tags.name: Captures
tags.description: Upload media against an existing verification. Two-stage flow: mint a presigned S3 URL → PUT bytes direct to S3 → POST submit-capture with the resulting key. Hardware attestation (Cloudflare Turnstile / Apple PAT) is verified per-capture.

tags.name: Public Trial
tags.description: Unauthenticated trial endpoint behind `rial.io/trial`. Each call mints a fresh verification under the rial. tenant tagged `originChannel="wa"`, so the WA-completion worker delivers the verdict to the configured trial number.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: Publish, update, revoke and inspect link templates — the reusable capture links behind `/l/{token}` (a compact JWT carrying the org and template slugs; the legacy `/l/{org}/{slug}` keeps resolving). Callable with a secret key; each publish snapshots a versioned capture spec (GET-83).

tags.name: Databases
tags.description: Create, update, inspect and synchronize tenant-scoped databases used by reusable verification templates. Callable with a dashboard session or secret API key.

cookieSession.name: rial_session
cookieSession.description: Dashboard / operator session cookie. Set by `/v1/auth/google/callback` after Google OAuth, JWT signed with the rotating `rial-platform/session-signing` HMAC. Read on every request the SPA makes with `credentials: include`. Browser-only — server-to-server callers use `bearerApiKey` instead.

bearerApiKey.description: Tenant-scoped API key (`pk_live_<ulid>`). Minted by a rial operator via the admin API; stored as SHA-256 hash, plaintext returns once at mint time. Use `Authorization: Bearer pk_live_<…>`. The presented key is hashed and looked up via the `gsi-by-key-hash` GSI on `rial-platform-tenants` — a hash miss returns 401 without timing channel.

captureToken.name: token
captureToken.description: Possession of the verification id in the URL path (`/v1/verifications/:token/...`) authenticates the SPA capture flow. No header — the id is the credential. ULIDs are large enough that existence-by-id is not a meaningful leak. Used for `POST /captures/upload-url`, `POST /captures`, `GET /v1/verify/:token`.

botHmac.name: X-Bot-Auth
botHmac.description: HMAC signature from the rialclaw WhatsApp bot. Signs `<timestamp>.<body>` with one of the secrets in `rial-platform/<stage>/bot-hmac` (comma-separated for rotation overlap). Required header pair: `X-Bot-Auth: <hex-hmac>` + `X-Bot-Auth-Timestamp: <unix-ms>`. Tenant id is carried in the request body, not in the credential.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `pending` → first capture flips to `partially_captured` → analysis sets the verdict and transitions to `completed`. Terminal: `completed`, `expired`, `failed`. `abandoned` is a side-branch off `pending`/`partially_captured`, reported by the capture screen via `POST /v1/verifications/:token/progress` when the end user leaves before finishing — NOT terminal: a later capture resurrects the row to `partially_captured` like any other.

max_captures.description: Derived total capacity (sum of steps[].max). `steps` is the authoritative spec.

items.description: One slot of the capture spec — a discriminated union on `type`. IMAGE slots: `key` is the stable slot id echoed back as `step_key` on every capture; `description` is the instruction shown to the person capturing; `min`/`max` bound how many captures the slot takes (`min: 0` = optional slot). `expected_object` optionally scopes the object check to that slot (operator responses only). `allow_upload: true` adds a file-upload fallback to the same image step; its optional `accept` and `max_size_bytes` use the upload defaults (all supported images and 10 MB, hard cap 25 MB). TEXT slots are declared form fields answered on the capture page: `required` gates completion, `validation` is declarative and bounded (length bounds + an enumerated format — `numeric_id` digits only, `alphanumeric_id` letters/digits/hyphens, `email` a valid address up to 254 characters; no arbitrary regex). UPLOAD slots are filled with preexisting content the client uploads instead of capturing live. VIDEO slots are live clips recorded in the moment through the capture page; `max_duration_sec` defaults to 30 and is hard-capped at 30.
A fraud-signal the tenant requires for the verification to count as complete.

mode.description: Echo of the `mode` the verification was created with. `audit` marks a run whose evidence is preexisting content pushed via API rather than captured live by a device — `steps` cannot stand in for it, since an audited file fills an ordinary `image` slot. Absent when the mint did not set it.

context.description: Free-form context the tenant attaches at issue time. The analysis pipeline cross-references this against what is observed in the capture (the `context_match` signal). Shape is identical to the aiornot-proxy `/reports/cross-check` `context` field — reuse, not translation.

completion_message.description: Full plain-text message shown after submitting content. HTML, markdown and variables are not interpreted. Omit on create or send null on PATCH to use the default.

expected_location.description: Address the captures are expected to happen at; activates presence verification (`location_match`).

location_required.description: Location is mandatory without a compare target: the run’s first capture must carry a fix or the capture endpoint rejects it (422 `location_required`). Set via `requires_location` at create time or by the minting link template. Never present alongside `expected_location`, which implies the demand on its own.

expected_object.description: Free-text description of the object the content must show; activates the object check (`object_match`).

condition_aspects.description: Free-form tenant-defined aspect names the condition check scores — any language, any domain, no fixed vocabulary (1..6 items, each non-empty and ≤40 chars); activates `condition`.

config.description: Tenant-supplied configuration baked into the token at issue time. Immutable after creation — changing config means issuing a new verification. `steps` is the normalized capture spec: requests that sent `max_captures: N` read back as a single anonymous step `{ key: "capture_1", min: N, max: N }`.

additionalProperties.description: One answered text step. `value` is USER-DECLARED — typed by the person capturing; unlike live-captured content, it is never sensor-attested. Potential PII: it rides the operator/developer contracts and the webhook only, never OG cards or third-party public surfaces.

record_seal.description: Integrity seal over the verification record including `answers`. Present only when answers exist and sealing is on (`seal !== false`). The hash proves the stored answers have not changed — it does NOT claim they are true or sensor-attested; `answers_provenance` carries that distinction explicitly.

signals.description: Per-signal evidence behind the verdict. Each signal is either its evaluated shape, or `{ status: "not_applicable", reason: "uploaded_content" }` when the slot was never evaluated because the underlying content was uploaded rather than captured live — never rendered as a failure.

reason_code.description: Which signal drove a non-`verified` label, in priority order (screen > AI > context > reverse search > depth) when more than one tripped. Absent on `verified` verdicts.

verdict.description: Aggregate verdict produced by the per-capture analysis pipeline. `label` is the human-readable bucket; `score` is the confidence in the verdict.

object_match.description: Object-check result. Present when an object check was requested globally or on an image step. With step-only configuration the status is the worst step result and expected_object is omitted. Independent of the fraud verdict.

additionalProperties.description: Object-check result for one image step, including its expected object.

object_matches.description: Object-check results keyed by image step. Missing capture verdicts yield inconclusive; otherwise each value is the worst context result for the step, ignoring not_applicable when live evidence exists.

items.description: One scored aspect of the condition assessment. `name` echoes the free-form tenant-defined aspect from `condition_aspects` verbatim — any language, any domain, no fixed vocabulary. `score` is 0..10 with one decimal; `reasoning` is a one-or-two-sentence visual justification.

One scored aspect of the condition assessment. `name` echoes the free-form tenant-defined aspect from `condition_aspects` verbatim — any language, any domain, no fixed vocabulary. `score` is 0..10 with one decimal; `reasoning` is a one-or-two-sentence visual justification.

additionalProperties.description: Condition assessment. Present only when the verification was created with `condition_aspects` — the free-form tenant-defined aspect names (any language, any domain). `score` is the one-decimal average of aspect scores; `label` buckets it (>=7.5 good, >=5 fair, else poor). Independent of the fraud verdict.

steps.description: Condition results keyed by photo step. Each uses only that step’s photos and its rubric, falling back to the shared rubric. The aggregate averages all assessed aspect scores.

condition.description: Condition assessment. Present only when the verification was created with `condition_aspects` — the free-form tenant-defined aspect names (any language, any domain). `score` is the one-decimal average of aspect scores; `label` buckets it (>=7.5 good, >=5 fair, else poor). Independent of the fraud verdict.

screen.description: Worst-case across sampled frames: one flagged frame flags the clip; `decided_at_ms` is the clip position of the deciding frame.

video_analysis.description: Screen-detection analysis of a video-step clip, sampled at one frame per second. Written asynchronously after capture — poll or use webhooks; absent until the worker has run.

progress.description: Latest funnel-progress snapshot reported via `POST /v1/verifications/:token/progress`. A snapshot, not an event log — each call overwrites the previous one. Operator-only; never present on the public projection.

Verification.description: Canonical wire shape for a verification. `narrative` is present after finalize; an empty value marks submission through `POST /v1/verifications/{token}/complete`. `verdict` is present only after analysis completed.

ErrorResponse.description: Uniform error envelope. `code` is the stable string SDKs branch on (`invalid_request`, `unauthorized`, `not_found`, `expired`, `step_full`, `unknown_step`, `steps_incomplete`, `already_finalized`, `too_many_requests`, `storage_unavailable`, `internal_error`). `fields` is only present on `invalid_request` validation failures.

completion_message.description: Full plain-text message shown after submitting content. HTML, markdown and variables are not interpreted. Omit on create or send null on PATCH to use the default.

CreateVerificationRequest.description: Body for `POST /v1/verifications`. All fields optional — sensible defaults: `max_captures: 1`, `expires_in_seconds: 3600`, `signals_required: ["screen", "ai"]`. Capture quantity comes as EITHER `max_captures` (N anonymous captures) OR `steps` (guided slots with key/description/min/max) — never both. `context` is what the analysis pipeline cross-references against the capture; `metadata` is opaque pass-through echoed back on every webhook event.

FinalizeVerificationRequest.description: Body for `POST /v1/verifications/:id/finalize`. `narrative` is the claimant's written description of what the captures show.

RequestUploadUrlRequest.description: Body for `POST /v1/verifications/:token/captures/upload-url`. The returned presigned PUT URL is single-use, 5-minute TTL, locked to the specified `contentType` — a stolen URL cannot be repurposed for a different mime.

completion_message.description: Full plain-text message shown after submitting content. HTML, markdown and variables are not interpreted. Omit on create or send null on PATCH to use the default.

csv.description: Raw CSV text, header row first.

column_mapping.description: Optional explicit header→field mapping when automap falls short.

items.description: 1-based CSV row (header is row 1) and why it was rejected.

post.description: Mints a verification the tenant's end-user redeems by submitting content against the returned `capture_url`. The configuration (capture spec, required fraud signals, optional tenant `context`, optional `webhook_url`, optional `notify_email`) is immutable after issue — to change anything, issue a new verification. When the request omits `notify_email`, the tenant's account-level default (configured from the dashboard's Integrations screen) is stamped into the config at mint time. An explicit request value always wins: a string targets that address, `notify_email: null` opts this verification out of email entirely. Changing the account default only affects future tokens.

201.description: Verification minted. Returns the canonical wire shape including the `capture_url` the tenant sends to the end-user.

401.description: No valid session / API key / bot HMAC.

402.description: plan_limit_reached or insufficient_credits: monthly plan quota and legacy credits cannot cover another image.

429.description: Tenant rate limit exceeded. Response carries `Retry-After: <seconds>` per RFC 7231.

error.message: Rate limit exceeded for this tenant. Retry after the specified interval.

get.summary: List (and search) tenant verifications, newest first
get.description: Newest-first list, opaque-cursor paginated. `next_cursor` from the previous page round-trips back as `?cursor=`; absent means the list is exhausted.

schema.description: Soft cap; adapters may return fewer.
Opaque cursor from a previous response. Treat as a black box.
Exact match on `verdict.label`. Pending verifications never match.
Exact match on `verdict.reason_code`. Verifications with no verdict, or a `verified` verdict, never match.
Inclusive lower bound on `created_at`. ISO 8601 date or date-time.
Inclusive upper bound on `created_at`. ISO 8601 date or date-time.
Exact match against `config.metadata[<key>]`. Repeatable with different keys (ANDed). Literal param name is `metadata.` followed by the metadata key, e.g. `metadata.client_label=estancia-la-julia`.
Exact match against `ocr.primary` of any capture on the verification.

Provenance split. `audit` matches `config.mode = audit` or an upload-only step spec (link-template audits that never stamp `mode`). `verification` is everything else — live capture, including rows that omit `mode`.

200.description: A page of verifications matching the filters. `next_cursor` absent means no more pages.

items.narrative: Front bumper damaged after low-speed collision in supermarket parking lot.

400.description: An explicit search filter (`status`, `verdict`, `reason_code`, `from`, `to`, `mode`) was malformed.

get.summary: Fetch a verification with its captures
get.description: Returns the verification and every capture submitted against it (inlined). Capture `image_url` fields are presigned with a 1-hour TTL — the dashboard can drop them into `` with no auth handshake. The S3 bucket policy itself stays private.

200.description: Verification including inlined captures with presigned image URLs.

example.narrative: Front bumper damaged after low-speed collision in supermarket parking lot.

404.description: Unknown id OR id belongs to a different tenant (channel-hidden).

get.summary: Public verification projection for the certificate page
get.description: No auth required. Returns a **narrower** projection than `/v1/verifications/:id` — strips operator-only fields (attestation, telemetry, internal capture metadata). Audience is the public reader of `rial.io/v/:id` confirming a completed verification certificate.

200.description: Public-safe projection of a completed verification.

get.description: Every domain event the worker recorded against this verification, in chronological order. Powers the dashboard "Audit timeline" card. Read-only.

200.description: Audit entries in chronological order.

post.summary: Close a verification with the claimant narrative
post.description: Attaches the claimant's written `narrative` to the verification and closes the case. The narrative is an operator surface: it is stored and returned on the operator audience, never on the developer (API-key) one.

example.narrative: Front bumper damaged after low-speed collision in supermarket parking lot. Photos taken immediately after, then again at the workshop the next morning.

200.description: Verification closed. Response is the updated verification with `narrative` now present.

example.narrative: Front bumper damaged after low-speed collision in supermarket parking lot.

400.description: Narrative missing, empty, or > 2KB. `fields` carries the Zod validation issues.

fields.message: String must contain at most 2000 character(s)

409.description: Case already finalized (narrative set) OR verification in terminal status (`completed`/`expired`/`failed`).

error.message: Verification case has already been finalized

post.description: Call after all answers and files have been submitted. Required for grouped or conditional steps and when optional files are omitted. Validates the currently visible required fields and evidence minimums, locks further answers and uploads, and queues analysis. Repeating the call is safe; retry a 503 to requeue analysis. The token in the path is the credential. A successful response acknowledges submission; poll the verification or receive its webhook for the final verdict.

200.description: Submitted; analysis may still be running.

409.description: Required visible steps are incomplete, or the verification failed.

503.description: Temporary storage or event delivery failure; retry the same request.

post.summary: Mint a presigned S3 URL the client uploads bytes to
post.description: Stage 1 of the upload flow. Returns a single-use presigned PUT URL (5-minute TTL, locked to the specified `contentType`) the SPA / SDK uploads raw bytes to. Bypassing the Lambda avoids the 6 MB sync-invocation cap; the Lambda only sees the resulting `image_key` reference on stage 3 (`POST /captures`).

200.description: Presigned URL minted. Client PUTs bytes here next.

post.summary: Submit a capture against the verification
post.description: Stage 3 of the upload flow (or stage 1 for inline-base64 payloads ≤ 6 MB). Two body shapes, discriminated by which field is present:

201.description: Capture persisted. Returns the updated verification — status will be `partially_captured` until the worker writes the verdict.

400.description: Invalid body, sha256 mismatch, or an unknown step key (`unknown_step` — `step_key` references a nonexistent or non-evidence step).

409.description: The target step already holds its maximum captures (`step_full`). With `max_captures` sugar this is the old "quota exhausted" case; with explicit `steps` it is per slot.

error.message: Step "capture_1" has already received its maximum number of captures

422.description: The verification demands a location fix and this is the first capture of the run, but it carries none (`location_required`). Nothing was persisted; collect a geolocation fix and resubmit.

error.message: This verification requires the device location — the first capture must carry a geolocation fix

post.summary: Answer one form step of the capture spec
post.description: Submit the answer to a text, choice, or address step of the verification's `steps`. Same trust model as `/captures`: the path's token is the credential.

200.description: Answer persisted. Returns the updated verification.

400.description: Invalid body, unknown step key (`unknown_step`), or a value that fails the step's declared validation.

409.description: Verification already reached a terminal status — answers are immutable (`answers_closed`).

error.message: Verification is closed — answers can no longer be submitted

post.description: Best-effort telemetry from the hosted-capture screen — powers "know when/where someone abandons a verification". Same trust model as `/captures`/`/answers`: the path's token is the credential.

204.description: Snapshot stored (and, when applicable, status flipped to `abandoned`).

410.description: Verification expired (`expires_at` < now) — only for `kind` other than `abandoned`; an abandoned-kind call on an expired token still returns `204`.

post.description: Powers the `rial.io/trial` QR-driven landing flow. Each visit mints a fresh verification under the rial. tenant (`tnt_rial`) tagged `originChannel='wa'` so the WA-completion worker delivers the verdict to the configured trial phone number once the user uploads a photo.

200.description: Trial verification minted. `capture_url` is the SPA URL the visitor opens to upload their photo.

429.description: Per-IP rate limit exceeded (1000 req/h). `Retry-After` header set.

get.summary: Resolve a permanent short template link
get.description: Resolves the opaque 10-character code in `/l/{code}`. Returns the slug landing payload plus `org` and `tpl` for the existing start endpoint. Paused links return 200 with status `paused`. Codes never expire or change on template rename. No state token is issued.

200.description: Template landing and slugs for starting a verification.

404.description: Uniform not found response for unknown links, drafts and unavailable tenants.

get.summary: Resolve a template link by slugs
get.description: Also used by legacy `/l/{org}/{tpl}` links and both permanent JWT link vintages. Previous template slugs remain aliases after a rename. When assigned, `short_code` is the stable resume identity shared by all link shapes.

200.description: Template landing.

404.description: Uniform not found response for unknown links, drafts and unavailable tenants.

get.description: Newest-first list of the tenant's published templates, each with live `started_total` / `started_today` counters.

200.description: All templates for the tenant.

503.description: The template store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

post.description: Creates the template and its public link in one step — the link starts `active` (unless `status: "paused"` is sent) at `/l/{token}` — `public_url`, whose single path segment is a compact JWT carrying the org and template slugs (the legacy `/l/{org}/{slug}` keeps resolving). The published snapshot starts at `version: 1` (GET-83); every verification minted from the link records the version it ran against.

completion_message.description: Full plain-text message shown after submitting content. HTML, markdown and variables are not interpreted. Omit on create or send null on PATCH to use the default.

201.description: Template published. `version` is always `1` on create.

400.description: Body failed validation (slug charset, steps not mintable, mode incoherent).

409.description: Slug already taken by a live template of this tenant.

422.description: `brand_slug` references a brand profile that does not exist for the tenant.

503.description: The template store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

patch.summary: Update a template (pause/resume, caps, republish snapshot)
patch.description: Partial update. Two classes of field behave differently (GET-83):

completion_message.description: Full plain-text message shown after submitting content. HTML, markdown and variables are not interpreted. Omit on create or send null on PATCH to use the default.

200.description: Updated template — `version` reflects whether the patch touched the snapshot.

400.description: Body failed validation or `steps` incoherent with the persisted `mode`.

404.description: No template with that slug for the authenticated tenant.

422.description: `brand_slug` references a brand profile that does not exist for the tenant.

503.description: The template store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

delete.description: Deletes the record and frees the slug. The public link starts returning 404 immediately; verifications already minted from it are untouched.

200.description: Template revoked.

404.description: No template with that slug for the authenticated tenant.

503.description: The template store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

post.description: Dry-run of `POST /v1/link-templates/{slug}/import` (GET-69/B6): parses the CSV, reports the resolved column mapping, row counts and per-row problems. Persists NOTHING — no job, no file, no worker trigger. The dashboard always calls this before submit so a bad file (wrong column, typo'd header) is caught before the 20%-invalid abort rule can kill a whole batch.

200.description: Parse report — resolved mapping, valid/invalid rows, abort prediction.

items.description: 1-based CSV row (header is row 1) and why it was rejected.

404.description: No template with that slug for the authenticated tenant.

503.description: The template store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

post.description: Validates, persists an `ImportJob` + the raw CSV, and triggers the background worker — the 202 is a receipt, not a result: ZERO verifications are minted in this request. Poll `GET /v1/link-templates/imports/{jobId}` for progress.

200.description: Identical bytes already submitted — the EXISTING job is returned with `duplicate: true`; nothing re-runs.

202.description: Import job accepted — the worker mints verifications asynchronously.

items.description: 1-based CSV row (header is row 1) and why it was rejected.

404.description: No template with that slug for the authenticated tenant.

503.description: The template store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

get.description: Progress of an async CSV import: `processing` → `completed` | `failed` | `aborted`, with bounded per-row errors (`invalid_rows` is capped at import time so this response never grows unbounded).

200.description: Current job state.

404.description: No template with that slug for the authenticated tenant.

503.description: The template store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

post.summary: Simulate the template (mint a sandbox verification)
post.description: Mints ONE verification from the template's current snapshot, flagged `simulation: true` — the async capture→worker→verdict pipeline runs for real, but the run is excluded from billable side effects: it does NOT count toward `GET /v1/me/usage` and does NOT fire tenant notifications.

201.description: Sandbox verification minted from the snapshot.

404.description: No template with that slug for the authenticated tenant.

429.description: Daily simulation cap for this template or tenant exhausted.

503.description: The template store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

get.description: Newest-first, each with its full `columns` + `rows` — callers can preview checks and seed batch imports without a per-cell round trip. The rows are tenant PII and never reach public verification reads.

200.description: All saved tables for the tenant.

503.description: The store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

post.description: The body carries the ALREADY-PARSED table (`columns` + `rows`); the dashboard parses and previews the CSV client-side. Limits: 5000 rows, 60 columns, 500 chars per cell, 1 MB total.

400.description: Body failed validation (duplicate columns, misaligned rows, limits).

409.description: The id already exists for this tenant.

503.description: The store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

put.description: Swaps the table WHOLE (name + columns + rows) under the same id — template bindings point at the id, so a re-upload must never rotate it. Bindings reference columns by NAME: a re-upload that keeps a column's name keeps every check pointed at it.

200.description: Table replaced — same `id`, same `created_at`, fresh `updated_at`.

404.description: No database with that id for the authenticated tenant.

503.description: The store is unreachable — retry with backoff.

patch.summary: Rename a saved table without replacing its snapshot

200.description: Renamed database.

404.description: No database with that id for the authenticated tenant.

503.description: The store is unreachable — retry with backoff.
